clue.text: Clumsy boat close to sewage pipe

parts.note: a tub is a slow, awkward, broad-beamed vessel

indicators.note: the close of something is its finish, so only the final letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ungainly vessel moored near the outflow from the sewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near' in the picture, but it means the end letter of the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube is a hollow cylinder carrying liquid or gas, which is exactly what a pipe is.

clue.text: Speculate the old get promoted

parts.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old
to rise is to go up in rank

explanation.surface: Guessing that the senior staff will be moved up the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' looks like a noun phrase for elderly people; it splits into THE plus O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form ideas or conjectures without proof, the same activity as guessing about something.

clue.text: Lancaster possibly welcoming small spell of increased activity

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Burt Lancaster was a Hollywood film star; 'possibly' flags the first name as one example of a Lancaster
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A Lancaster bomber, perhaps, briefly taking on a small extra crew during a busy period.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster suggests the city, the royal house or the wartime bomber; here it is the actor Burt Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst is a sudden short period of intense effort, as in a burst of energy or a burst of speed.

clue.text: Tea not elaborate for college minister

parts.note: cha is a British slang word for tea
plain means simple, unadorned

explanation.surface: A simple afternoon tea laid on for the college's resident clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is old British slang for tea, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleges, schools and hospitals appoint a chaplain, a clergyman who ministers to that institution's community.

clue.text: Hour on a bare rostrum unsettled port official

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hour

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed and no longer in its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone standing for an hour on a wobbly, bare platform, like an official addressing the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places H above the rest; the rostrum is not a lookout but anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbourmaster is the officer in charge of a port's harbour, regulating berths, shipping movements and safety.

clue.text: Establish factory

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to set something firmly in place

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words sound like an order to set up a factory; they are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to fix or found firmly; as a noun it is industrial premises with heavy machinery.

clue.text: Fool say, regularly manic, pointed weapon

parts.note: an ass is a silly person
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example', which is what 'say' means

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A crazed fool, as it were, brandishing something sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is not speech here but the exemplifying EG.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa, notably by Zulu warriors.

clue.text: Number no German mentioned

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken out loud, so the answer is identified by its sound

parts.note: nein is the German for no

explanation.surface: A tally in which no German person was named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No German' suggests counting zero Germans; it is the German word for no.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a whole number, the integer that comes after eight and before ten.

clue.text: Bad luck: his map is faulty

indicators.note: a faulty thing is defective or wrongly put together, so the letters need reassembling

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's misfortune is blamed on a badly drawn map.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a complete story of blame, but 'his map' is simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident, a small piece of misfortune that goes wrong.

clue.text: Previous title-holder that is first to resign

parts.note: an earl holds a noble title
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The former champion was the first to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title-holder' suggests a sporting champion, but it is a nobleman; 'that is' gives IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier and previous both describe something that came before in time or order.

clue.text: Right for a child to admit crime

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a son is a child
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Is it proper for a youngster to confess to an offence?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' suggests confessing, but it means letting R into A SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a specific criminal offence.

clue.text: Gag miserable person told

indicators.note: something told is spoken to a listener, so we go by the sound, not the spelling

parts.note: a wretch is an unhappy, unfortunate person

explanation.surface: Silence the unhappy fellow who has been informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' reads as silencing someone, but it is the involuntary throat movement; the W of the sound-alike is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag and to retch both mean making the spasmodic throat movement of vomiting without bringing anything up.

clue.text: Losing heart, violent anger in power cut

indicators.note: losing your heart means losing your centre, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: outrage is fierce indignation

explanation.surface: Furious at losing electricity, someone's spirit gives out.
explanation.walkthrough: OUTRAGE has seven letters, so its heart is the single middle R.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a period when electricity or another utility supply fails, which is exactly a power cut.

clue.text: Split Cambridgeshire city in a serious way

parts.note: to sever is to cut apart
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, in eastern England

explanation.surface: A city in eastern England divided in a grave fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city near Cambridge, a crossword favourite because of its convenient letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely is an adverb meaning gravely, harshly or to a serious degree.

clue.text: Cheating in keen exercise

parts.note: keen and sharp both describe a fine cutting edge
an exercise is a piece of practice

explanation.surface: Someone cuts corners during an enthusiastic training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but it is the keen of a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is an idiom for dishonest or barely legal dealing to gain an advantage, a form of cheating.

clue.text: Relatives eating second helpings

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: aunts are family members
a mo is British slang for a moment, a short time like a second

explanation.surface: Family members tucking into a second plateful at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second helpings' looks like one phrase but breaks after 'second'; 'Just a mo' is British slang for 'just a second'.
explanation.definitionFit: A helping is a portion, a quantity of food served, so amounts is a looser synonym.

clue.text: The opera for motor mechanics?

parts.note: surface reading: which opera would garage workers enjoy?
setter's reading: people who work on automobiles could be called by a two-word name, and that name, run together, is the title of Bizet's opera

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: split the opera's name into two words and they describe men who work with cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's 1875 opera about a fiery Seville gypsy woman is one of the most performed operas in the world.

clue.text: Record odd bits of guitar in open-sided room

parts.note: a log is a written record, as on a ship

indicators.note: the odd-numbered positions are the first, third and fifth, so only those letters are kept

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word

explanation.surface: Recording some guitar on a veranda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests making a recording, but it is a written log.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is an Italian architectural term for a gallery or room open to the air on one or more sides.

clue.text: Good space for man of the match

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
room means available space

explanation.surface: Plenty of room for the best player in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the match' is the award for a game's best player, but here the match is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is also a marriage, and the groom is the man being married at a wedding.

clue.text: Stratagem to store energy for recycling

indicators.note: storing something keeps it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or scheme
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A clever scheme for storing energy so it can be used again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like green technology; 'store' really means holding the letter E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Reuse, as a noun, is using something again rather than discarding it, which is what recycling means.

clue.text: College working for merger

parts.note: uni is short for university
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A college working towards amalgamation with another.
explanation.walkthrough: UNI is the everyday British short form of university.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is the joining of two or more things into one, the same idea as an amalgamation of companies.

clue.text: Knocks up something for a mast

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks

explanation.surface: Someone hammering together a pole to serve as a mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks up' reads as a phrasal verb for building something quickly; it splits into a word and a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole used in a ship's rigging, such as a mast, yard or boom.

clue.text: Gasp over Christmas show

parts.note: to pant is to breathe in gasps
O stands for over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An audience gasping at a festive performance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A panto, short for pantomime, is a British family comedy theatre show staged at Christmas, full of slapstick and audience participation.

clue.text: Similar things in article to enjoy

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article
to like something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: Finding comparable pleasures in a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: 'And the like' is an idiom meaning other comparable items, so the phrase stands for such things.

clue.text: Mount is to gallop further

definitions.note: the answer is the name that follows 'Mount' in the full place name

parts.note: to rush is to move very fast
more means additional, further

explanation.surface: Get on the horse in order to ride on faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' reads as climbing onto a horse, which suits galloping, but it is the start of a mountain's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota bears the carved heads of four US presidents, so the answer completes that name.

clue.text: Just love end of fall in New York

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: NY is the standard abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so just that one is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Simply adoring the close of autumn in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' is the American word for autumn, apt with New York, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only are adverb synonyms meaning merely or no more than.
